cards.q: What is exposure bias in standard supervised Knowledge Distillation ($\lambda = 0$)?
cards.a: During offline KD, the student only sees gold/teacher prefixes, but at inference it conditions on its own imperfect tokens, entering unfamiliar states where errors compound.

cards.q: How does On-Policy GKD ($\lambda > 0$) fix exposure bias without needing ground-truth reward verifiers?
cards.a: With probability $\lambda$, the student generates its own rollout $y \sim p_\theta(\cdot|x)$, and the teacher provides dense per-token probability targets $p_T(\cdot | x, y_{<t})$ on the exact states the student actually visits.

cards.q: How do Forward KL ($D_{\text{KL}}(P_T \parallel P_S)$) and Reverse KL ($D_{\text{KL}}(P_S \parallel P_T)$) differ in behavior?
cards.a: Forward KL is mode-covering (penalizes student wherever $P_T > 0$, spreading mass across all teacher modes). Reverse KL is mode-seeking (penalizes student wherever $P_T \approx 0$, locking onto the teacher's single sharpest mode).

cards.q: Why does raising distillation temperature $T > 1$ help a smaller student learn from teacher logits?
cards.a: Dividing logits by $T > 1$ softens the distribution and boosts "dark knowledge" in runner-up tokens, teaching relative token similarities instead of a near-one-hot argmax.

cards.q: What is the geometric formula connecting the dot product $a \cdot b$ to cosine similarity?
cards.a: $a \cdot b = \|a\|_2 \|b\|_2 \cos\theta$, so cosine similarity is $\frac{a \cdot b}{\|a\|_2 \|b\|_2}$, which removes vector lengths and compares direction only.

cards.q: Why does $L_1$ regularization produce sparse (exact-zero) weights while $L_2$ weight decay does not?
cards.a: The derivative of $w^2$ is $2w$ (which vanishes near $0$), whereas the derivative of $|w|$ is $\pm 1$ all the way to $0$, pushing small weights to exact zero.

cards.q: If $Y = XW$ with $X$ of shape $(B, d_{\text{in}})$ and $W$ of shape $(d_{\text{in}}, d_{\text{out}})$, what are the backprop shapes for $dX$ and $dW$?
cards.a: $dX = dY\,W^\top$ has shape $(B, d_{\text{out}}) \times (d_{\text{out}}, d_{\text{in}}) \to (B, d_{\text{in}})$, and $dW = X^\top dY$ has shape $(d_{\text{in}}, B) \times (B, d_{\text{out}}) \to (d_{\text{in}}, d_{\text{out}})$.

cards.q: How many parameters and what maximum rank does a LoRA update $\Delta W = B A$ have when $B$ is $(d, r)$ and $A$ is $(r, d)$?
cards.a: It has $2dr$ parameters (instead of $d^2$) and rank at most $r$, because every input passes through an $r$-dimensional bottleneck.

cards.q: What is an eigenvector $v$ and eigenvalue $\lambda$ of a square matrix $A$ in plain geometry?
cards.a: A direction $v$ that does not rotate when multiplied by $A$ ($Av = \lambda v$); $A$ simply stretches or shrinks $v$ by the factor $\lambda$.

cards.q: In the multivariable chain rule, when do you multiply local derivatives vs. add them?
cards.a: You multiply local derivatives along a sequential chain ($w \to z \to \hat{y} \to L$), and you add derivatives whenever a variable branches to feed multiple downstream paths.

cards.q: What is the derivative of $\sigma(z)$, and why does it cause vanishing gradients in deep networks?
cards.a: $\sigma'(z) = \sigma(z)(1 - \sigma(z))$, which is at most $0.25$ (at $z = 0$) and near $0$ for large $|z|$. Multiplying numbers $\le 0.25$ across many layers shrinks gradients exponentially.

cards.q: What is the gradient $\frac{\partial L}{\partial z}$ of Cross-Entropy loss combined with Sigmoid or Softmax logits $z$?
cards.a: $\frac{\partial L}{\partial z} = \hat{p} - y$ (predicted probability minus true label), because the $1/\hat{p}$ derivative of $-\ln \hat{p}$ cancels the $\hat{p}(1 - \hat{p})$ factor from sigmoid/softmax.

cards.q: If a loss valley has second-derivative curvature $h = L''(w) > 0$, what is the optimal 1-step learning rate and the maximum stable learning rate?
cards.a: Optimal 1-step Newton learning rate is $\eta = 1/h$; maximum stable learning rate before steps overshoot and diverge is $\eta_{\max} = 2/h$.
